title: Security posture discovery with Polaris Security
header: Date: 2026-03-26 | Time: 16:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Polaris CTO), Sofia Martinez (Polaris Head of InfoSec), Ravi Singh (Polaris SRE)
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
summary: Intro discovery focused on security posture and compliance needs. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private options; primary concerns: SOC2 attestation, SSO/SAML, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs/retention, KMS integration, and data residency. Next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 report & ISO summary, schedule SE deep dive for network/VPC and performance, and provide example RBAC/SCIM docs and pilot proposal.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Ethan our SE.
[00:08] Liam (Polaris): Hi all, Liam here, CTO. We're evaluating vendors for inference - security is our gating factor.
[00:14] Sofia (Polaris): Sofia, Head of InfoSec. Couple quick asks up front: SOC 2, ISO 27001, SSO, audit logs, KMS.
[00:20] Ethan (Redwood): Absolutely, that's what we wanted to cover. We'll walk through our posture and clarifying Qs around data flows and retention.
[00:30] Maya: Quick note - we'll capture action items; apologies in advance if the transcript messes up some product names, we've seen that.
[00:36] Sofia: Great. On SOC 2 - do you have a current Type II report? How often?
[00:42] Ethan: Yes, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II annually, most recent was late 2025. We can share the artifacts under an NDA. The report covers our hosted control plane and operational controls plus access logging.
[00:55] Sofia: And ISO 27001?
[00:58] Ethan: We're ISO-aligned and engaging cert process for 2026; we have the scoping and the gap analysis done - we can provide the statement of applicability and our roadmap.
[01:08] Ravi: From an infra perspective, we run some workloads in dedicated pools for customers and we need to know network isolation - can you do VPC peering or private link?
[01:17] Ethan: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private link options depending on cloud provider; for Private we can provide a customer-managed control plane in their VPC or an on-prem package. There's some nuance on egress and management plane traffic, we'll need a technical session to map ports and IP ranges.
[01:32] Liam: Important for us: minimal cross-tenant blast radius. How is tenant isolation enforced?
[01:37] Maya: Good question. For Hosted we use logical isolation with strict RBAC, encryption at rest, and per-tenant keying options for higher tiers. Dedicated gives stronger isolation with dedicated GPU pools. Private gives full network and tenancy separation.
[01:50] Sofia: On RBAC - can you do roles mapped to our IdP via SCIM? We want groups like Admin, Dev, Auditor with fine-grained rights.
[01:58] Ethan: Yes - SSO via SAML or OIDC is supported. SCIM for user/group sync is available for Dedicated and Private customers today; hosted customers on enterprise plan can get SCIM. Roles are configurable and you'll be able to map groups to RBAC roles.
[02:12] Sofia: Audit logs - retention, immutability? We need 12 months retention and tamper-evident logs for compliance.
[02:19] Ethan: Audit logs are available at both organization and API-key level. Default retention is 90 days in hosted, but enterprise packages can extend to 12+ months. For immutability we support write-once storage exports to customer S3 and audit log streaming to SIEM via Kafka or AWS Kinesis. We can show example configs.
[02:38] Liam: Encryption - KMS integration? Customer-managed keys?
[02:42] Ethan: We support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we offer Google Cloud KMS / AWS KMS integrated, and for enterprise customers we can provide CMEK. Customer-managed HSM integrations (via partnership) are possible, will need deeper legal and architecture review.
[02:58] Sofia: Data residency - we have EU-only data flows for certain PII. Can you ensure data never leaves region?
[03:04] Maya: Yes. We have region routing - requests can be pinned to EU regions and we can restrict model variants to region-compliant endpoints. For full guarantee we'd recommend Dedicated or Private in-region deployment.
[03:16] Ravi: For logs and artifacts, is there a way to keep everything in our VPC?
[03:20] Ethan: For Private, yes. For Dedicated we can place logging endpoints in your VPC, and for Hosted we can forward logs to your ingestion endpoints or S3.
[03:29] Sofia: Can we get a sample of the SOC 2 report and the penetration test summary?
[03:33] Maya: Yes, we will share the redacted SOC 2 Type II and latest pentest exec summary under NDA.
[03:38] Liam: Performance question - we may start with Hosted for speed, but move to Dedicated when throughput grows. Is migration straightforward?
[03:45] Ethan: The API is consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Models and versions can be pinned, so migration is mostly infra and network. We usually run a staged cutover and support KV cache warming.
[03:57] Sofia: One more: data retention for prompts and outputs. We need configurable deletion and an auditing mechanism for retained prompts used for model improvement.
[04:06] Ethan: By default, hosted may retain for up to 30 days for abuse/quality monitoring; enterprise customers can opt-out of any retention or route data to their own storage. We also have data classification controls and suppression APIs to purge artifacts.
[04:22] Ravi: Are there role separation controls for operations vs security?
[04:26] Ethan: Yes - RBAC allows distinct roles and permissions. We also have approval workflows for sensitive actions, and audit trails on all admin ops.
[04:36] Sofia: What about SAML behaviour for multiple IdPs? We use Okta primarily but sometimes we have AD FS for legacy apps.
[04:44] Ethan: We support multiple IdP configs for one org and SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. SCIM provisioning will sync groups from Okta/AD as supported.
[04:54] Liam: Any known gaps we should plan for?
[04:57] Maya: The one area is fully air-gapped on-prem install - we offer an on-prem package but there are extra ops and legal items. We'll need to scope a project plan for that.
[05:07] Sofia: Okay. Let's talk timeline - we want compliance review and pilot before end of Q2.
[05:12] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll prepare the security packet and an SE deep-dive to map VPC requirements this week.
[05:18] Ethan: I'll propose times for a technical session to go over IP ranges, ports, and a small benchmark plan.
[05:24] Liam: Pricing and pilot specifics?
[05:27] Maya: We'll send a pilot proposal with pricing for hosted trial and an optional Dedicated pilot.
[05:32] Sofia: For the pilot, we'd like to test with our EU data subset and verify logs streaming to our SIEM.
[05:38] Ethan: Noted, we'll include SIEM integration steps.
[05:42] Maya: Any other questions?
[05:44] Ravi: One minor thing: do you integrate with our KMS key rotation policies?
[05:49] Ethan: Yes, we honor KMS key rotation and support key rotation patterns; we'll document the exact mechanism.
[05:55] Maya: Okay folks, recap and next steps coming out now. Thanks everyone.
[06:00] Sofia: Thanks.
[06:03] End of recording.

Note: transcription contains occasional label noise and short gaps; some product names maybe mistranscribed (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" might appear as "Redwood dedicate").
